## Cohort

The brca cohort consists of 1071 patients, with gene expression data available for 1069. A total of 18 patients are reported as unsequenced. The dataset was split into training (749 patients) and testing (322 patients) sets. Data quality checks, including split integrity, minimum events, leakage, proportional hazards, and convergence, all returned true, indicating a valid dataset. Missing data is present for several variables: 19 patients have missing ‘stage’ information (0.0177 fraction), and 18 patients each have missing data for ‘mut_TP53’, ‘mut_PIK3CA’, ‘mut_CDH1’, ‘mut_GATA3’, ‘mut_MAP3K1’, and ‘mut_KMT2C’ (0.0168 fraction each). Thirteen patients were excluded due to nonpositive overall survival times.

## Models and metrics

Four models were evaluated: Cox proportional hazards model with clinical data (cox/clinical), Random Survival Forest with clinical data (rsf/clinical), Cox proportional hazards model with clinical and expression data (cox/clinical_expression), and Random Survival Forest with clinical and expression data (rsf/clinical_expression). Performance was assessed using Harrell’s C, Integrated Brier Score (IBS), and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) at 12, 24, and 36-month time horizons.

Here's a summary of the key metrics:

| Model                     | Harrell's C | IBS    | AUC (12m) | AUC (24m) | AUC (36m) |
|--------------------------|-------------|--------|----------|----------|----------|
| cox/clinical             | 0.728       | 0.118  | 0.748    | 0.731    | 0.718    |
| rsf/clinical             | 0.741       | 0.112  | 0.761    | 0.746    | 0.731    |
| cox/clinical_expression | 0.728       | 0.117  | 0.743    | 0.728    | 0.716    |
| rsf/clinical_expression | 0.731       | 0.114  | 0.752    | 0.736    | 0.724    |

The rsf/clinical model demonstrates the highest Harrell’s C (0.741) and AUC values across all time horizons. The addition of expression data does not consistently improve performance, as evidenced by comparing cox/clinical and cox/clinical_expression, and rsf/clinical and rsf/clinical_expression.

## Checks and abstentions

All data quality checks – split integrity, minimum events, leakage, proportional hazards, and convergence – passed, indicating the validity of the models and analysis. The analysis is limited to the provided pre-computed models and metrics. No further exploration or model tuning was performed.

## Limitations

The analysis is limited by the presence of missing data for ‘stage’ and several mutation variables. The exclusion of 13 patients with nonpositive survival times and the unsequenced status of 18 patients may introduce bias. While the models demonstrate reasonable performance, the lack of substantial improvement with the inclusion of expression data suggests that other factors may be more influential in predicting survival outcomes.
